one_month_reasoning: No TT earnings in the window (Q4 reports late January 2027). Events to 2026-11-29: the US midterm election (Nov 3), October CPI (mid-November), peer prints (JCI fiscal Q4 in early/mid November, LII/AAON already out) and any hyperscaler capex commentary. The stock fell 8.6% (448.47 -> 410.00) on a revenue/bookings beat with only a reaffirmed EPS guide: implied Q4 EPS 3.40-3.50 vs the still-stale $3.59 Street (Nasdaq), FY price cut to ~1pt and leverage to low-20s. Negative post-guidance drift (estimates still to fall ~3-5% for Q4) roughly offsets short-term reversal after a sharp gap down near the 52-week range middle, so I centre slightly above spot (411.5) with the usual monthly vol 30%/3.5 = 8.6%, widened to 8.8% for post-earnings drift uncertainty.

fair_value.method: Quarterly segment build: FY27 revenue $26.8B (+10.6%), GAAP EBIT $5.0B (18.7%), FY28 $28.9B / $5.5B; NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) model EPS valued at 22.3x P/E (w 0.75) and LTM EBITDA at 19.5x (w 0.25), bridged with net debt and -1.5%/yr shares; engine base horizon value $444.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT (after SBC) in the build and GAAP-basis model EPS; share count falls only by net buybacks (-1.5%/yr). Peers' adjusted EPS mostly keep SBC expensed, so the basis matches.

reasoning: Started from the filings: Q3'26 revenue $6,760M (+18%), bookings $7,248M, backlog $12.5B (+73%), but EMEA/APAC margins -250/-390bp and the FY EPS guide only reaffirmed; the call put Q4 adjusted EPS at $3.40-3.50 (incl. 10c tax) vs a $3.59 Street still un-revised, cut FY price to ~1pt (from 1.5) and FY organic leverage to low-20s (from 25%+) - that is why a beat sold off 8.6%. The backlog says 2027 revenue is largely booked: >$8B of the $12.5B is for 2027+ and >$1B already for 2028, so FY27 Americas +11% needs only ~$7B of dated backlog plus flat-ish book-and-ship. I build segment revenue and GAAP margins quarter by quarter (seasonality = 2025-26 average shares), giving FY26 $24.2B (at the ~13.5% guide), FY27 $26.8B (+2.6% above pre-print consensus), FY28 $28.9B (+2% vs MarketScreener). Incrementals ~24% reported (below the 25% target: Stellar mix, low price). Model FY27 GAAP EPS ~$17.9 sits between Street $17.71 and whisper $18.10. Guidance record: every first annual EPS guide FY23-26 beaten (median +~6%); first revenue guides beaten 3 of 4. I still sit only at the top of the FY26 range (one quarter left) and below the 25% incremental target in FY27. Valuation: 7 genuine whole-company peers (flagged), NTM P/E median 19.5x; own 23.8x; k=0.8 exit 22.8x less 0.5 turn for the post-horizon data-center cycle = 22.3x (0.75 weight), plus an LTM GAAP EV/EBITDA cross-check at 19.5x (0.25). Downside (P10) = data-center orders pause + margin -200bp + de-rate to near the peer median; upside (P90) = faster burn, 25%+ incrementals, multiple held. Research was limited by sec.gov refusing scripted access without a contact email (filings read via WebFetch). All legs driver-linked; no custom legs.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Own NTM P/E 23.8x vs 19.5x median (+22%); exit P/E 22.3x after k=0.8 shrink and -0.5 turn for data-center cycle risk; EV/EBITDA LTM own 20.3x vs 16.7x, exit 19.5x
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium kept (k=0.8 rule) is consistent with structurally higher returns and margins than the HVAC median: GAAP operating margin 18.6% FY25 (F10/F3) vs low-teens for CARR/LII-type peers, backlog of $12.5B (+73%) giving 2027 visibility, and >100% FCF conversion. comps_summary.own_multiple_basis: P/E: 410 / Nasdaq consensus NTM (Q4'26 3.59 + Q1-Q3'27 3.15+5.02+5.49 = 17.25, adjusted); EV/EBITDA: trailing GAAP (F95) on the peers' filings basis
comps_summary.exit_rule: peer median x (own/median)^0.8; P/E less 0.5 turn (long_dated_risks)
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 7 whole-company peers (CARR, JCI, LII, AAON, SPXC, CSW, Daikin). No more genuine ones: Watsco (distributor) and Comfort Systems (contractor) are different models; VRT and MOD match only the data-center part (<25% of revenue) and are segment-only; China/Korea HVAC names (Gree, Midea, LG) excluded for country distortion; Nibe/others are heat-pump specialists in a downturn. EV/EBITDA rests on 3 peers with filing EBITDA (flag).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly segment driver build (Americas, EMEA, Asia Pacific revenue x GAAP segment operating margin, plus a cited corporate constant) for FY2026-28; value carried by an NTM P/E horizon multiple (0.75) on the build's own GAAP EPS and an LTM GAAP EV/EBITDA cross-check (0.25), both peer-anchored with the k=0.8 shrink. No DCF (not a neocloud), no SOTP (single-business HVAC; segments are geographic). Driven share of revenue 100%.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) the -0.5 turn on the exit P/E for post-horizon data-center cycle risk (~-2%, below the 5% card threshold); (2) the EV/EBITDA leg rests on 3 core peers' trailing GAAP multiples (thin); (3) P/E applies to model GAAP EPS, ~1.5% below adjusted EPS (backlog-amortisation add-back ~0.07/qtr), a small conservative bias vs the peers' adjusted consensus; (4) pending M&A (CanCoil + 2) size undisclosed: $400-500M/yr other_uses assumed. No financing event >=20% probability (net debt/EBITDA ~0.65x).
model_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 22.3x NTM P/E at the horizon on ~$20 EPS implies roughly 9-10% EPS growth for ~5 years after FY2028 with GAAP operating margins holding ~19%, i.e. data-center/applied demand normalising to replacement plus secular decarbonisation growth rather than collapsing.
